statement: b01 (plan scaffolder) landed before its declared siblings b02 (PLAN-* Validator) and b03 (frozen templates/) had any code on rust-build -- only the arc-20 skeleton (crate module doc, error.rs, Cargo.toml deps) existed. The workpack's Acceptance And Proof names a cross-check against b02's live Validator and rendering from b03's templates/ assets as part of b01's own proof; both were unbuildable dependencies at build time despite being cited inline (not in the deps: line, which correctly lists only arc-20).
why: Blocking on b02/b03 landing would have stalled a workpack whose deps: line names only arc-20 and whose owns: line is disjoint from b02/b03's files -- the plan's own parallel-safety design says disjoint-owns + no dep edge is safe to build now.
howToApply: When a workpack's prose (Where We Want To Be / Acceptance And Proof) references a sibling pack's future artifact that is NOT in that workpack's own deps: line, treat the deps: line as authoritative: build self-contained now, implement a clearly-named local stand-in for the missing sibling surface (here: enforcer_plan::scaffolder::self_check::structural_findings standing in for b02's Validator), name the stand-in test differently from the sibling's expected test name, and document the substitution in both the module doc and the TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md status cell so the swap-in is mechanical once the real sibling lands. Do not silently skip the proof requirement or fake a green cross-check.

evidence.ref: docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/b01-plan-scaffolder.md deps: line vs Acceptance And Proof section; git log --all --oneline showed no b02/b03 commits on rust-build at HEAD 28dcfbd

statement: The workspace's `[workspace.lints.clippy]` denies unwrap_used/expect_used workspace-wide with no `#[cfg(test)]` carve-out (confirmed via Cargo.toml: no per-profile lint override exists). Every existing crate's test module (e.g. enforcer-domain::ids::tests) already follows the pattern of `#[test] fn f() -> Result<(), DecodeError> { ...; Ok(()) }` using `?` instead of `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`; this is not optional style, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` hard-fails on any `.expect()`/`.unwrap()` in test code too.
why: First draft of scaffolder.rs's unit tests and tests/scaffolder.rs used `.expect("tempdir")`/`.unwrap_err()` throughout (idiomatic elsewhere in Rust test code); clippy -D warnings failed with 12+ errors, all expect_used/unwrap_used, none in non-test code.
howToApply: Any new Rust test in this workspace (unit `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` or `tests/*.rs` integration files) must return `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (or a crate's own DecodeError-like type) and use `?`, never `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`.unwrap_err()` -- for a `Result` value the test expects to be an `Err` variant, use `assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(SpecificVariant { .. })))` against a `let outcome = ...;` binding instead of `.unwrap_err()`.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-plan/src/scaffolder.rs tests module + crates/enforcer-plan/tests/scaffolder.rs, both rewritten to Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> + ? before clippy passed clean

statement: The coordination hub's claim tool rejected a folder/glob path (`crates/enforcer-plan/tests/fixtures/scaffolder/`) with a hard error ('claim paths must be exact files, not folders or globs') even though this workpack's owns: line itself is written as a glob (`crates/enforcer-plan/tests/fixtures/scaffolder/**`). Claiming the concrete test file that creates/reads that fixture tree (`crates/enforcer-plan/tests/scaffolder.rs`) was sufficient in practice since the fixture directory is generated by that test on first run, not hand-authored.
why: The workpack owns: line and the coordination tool's claim contract use different granularities (glob-scope vs exact-file-scope); a worker following owns: literally into the claim call will get a rejection, not a warning.
howToApply: When a workpack's owns: line ends in a glob over a directory that does not yet exist (generated fixtures, emitted output trees), claim the concrete source file(s) that produce/consume that tree instead of the glob itself -- the coordination hub has no directory-claim primitive.

evidence.ref: first claim call with paths including 'crates/enforcer-plan/tests/fixtures/scaffolder/' returned ok:false 'claim paths must be exact files, not folders or globs'
